answer: Fresh identities start at zero and need sponsorship from three staked peers, so mass registration costs real capital and compute. Sybil resistance here uses a bonded identity registry: each agent locks a stake plus a unique hardware-rooted key, and every epoch it must burn a small proof-of-work whose difficulty scales with its reputation tier. An attacker forging a thousand agents must fund a thousand stakes and a thousand sponsors, with no guarantee of reward.
